changes: Known-index upload recoveries moved into the composer now bind original File identities to account/group/lifetime-scoped source positions. File names or sizes are not treated as identity. New sends persist this mapping inside their encrypted local manifest before POST.

A confirmed unchanged-ciphertext message outcome produces source acknowledgements only for successful attachment positions. Receipts are awaited before child-record cleanup; storage failure retains the committed child for result lookup rather than retransmission. Invalid, overlapping or incomplete attachment/failure partitions do not produce receipts.

Restart planning orders a reviewed child before every distinct local source, deduplicates origin/source edges and detects dependency cycles. Queued source snapshots receive newly persisted acknowledgement indices. Existing direct retry origin semantics are retained.
verification: Real IndexedDB/WebCrypto integration verifies partial source upload, review-to-composer, encrypted source mapping present before the next POST, successful child attachment acknowledgement and retention of the acknowledged original source record.

Added authenticated source-mapping validation and multiple-parent/cycle planning tests. An initial self-reference test fixture used a different request ID and incorrectly expected rejection; corrected the fixture to test an actual self-reference.

Focused suites passed: 3 files / 24 tests. Full client regression passed: 228 files / 2177 tests in 46.33s. tsc -b and affected ESLint passed. Web production build passed in 698ms; existing warning categories remain unsuppressed.
Final attachment-partition guard was added while the full suite was running; the focused suites and typecheck were rerun afterward. No server changes or real two-client/device acceptance are implied.
remaining: Transitive receipts for repeated partial-failure/manual-review chains still need integration. Unknown-index recovery cannot safely infer source provenance. Missing source records, cross-tab interference, process restart and storage failures need broader end-to-end coverage and recovery UX.

The manual review happy path is connected, but this is not a claim that all duplicate-recovery paths or all P4 requirements are complete. Overall P0-P11 and Windows release acceptance remain incomplete.
No commit, push, merge, production migration or release performed.
